concepts.title: Hybridisation and Percentage s-Character of Carbon
concepts.definition: The hybridization state of carbon is determined by the mixing of valence s and p orbitals, where greater fractional s-character draws bonding electrons closer to the carbon nucleus, resulting in shorter and stronger bonds.
concepts.key_idea: Bond length decreases and carbon electronegativity increases as the s-character of the hybrid orbital increases.

solution_steps.action: determine total participating hybrid orbitals
solution_steps.explain: one s orbital mixes with p_orbitals to produce total hybrid orbitals

solution_steps.action: compute percentage of s-character
solution_steps.explain: divide the single s orbital by total orbitals and multiply by 100

solution_steps.action: relate the s-character percentage to bond length and electronegativity
solution_steps.explain: higher s-character shortens the C-H bond and increases carbon electronegativity, with sp at 50 percent being the strongest and shortest

concepts.title: Determination of Sigma and Pi Bonds in Organic Molecules
concepts.definition: Single covalent linkages represent coaxial sigma bonds, whereas multiple bonds consist of one sigma bond accompanied by one or two lateral-overlap pi bonds.
concepts.formula: total_sigma = sigma_cc + sigma_ch; total_bonds = total_sigma + pi_bonds
concepts.key_idea: Every single bond contributes one sigma bond; a double bond comprises one sigma and one pi; a triple bond contains one sigma and two pi bonds.

solution_steps.action: verify the bond count against the molecular structure
solution_steps.explain: cross-check that each single bond contributes one sigma, each double bond one sigma plus one pi, and each triple bond one sigma plus two pi bonds

concepts.title: Carbon Hybridisation and Molecular Geometry
concepts.definition: The spatial arrangement of bonds surrounding a carbon centre is governed by its hybridization, yielding tetrahedral geometry for sp3, planar triangular for sp2, and collinear linear geometry for sp.
concepts.key_idea: Carbon geometry is tetrahedral with 4 sigma bonds (sp3), trigonal planar with 3 sigma bonds (sp2), and linear with 2 sigma bonds (sp).

solution_steps.action: assign hybridization based on sigma bond tally
solution_steps.explain: 4 sigma bonds correspond to sp3, 3 to sp2, and 2 to sp

solution_steps.action: correlate hybridization to spatial geometry
solution_steps.explain: sp3 corresponds to tetrahedral, sp2 to trigonal planar, and sp to linear geometry

concepts.title: Condensed and Bond-Line Structural Representations
concepts.definition: Chemical formulas can be depicted in full form showing every bond, condensed by grouping identical repeating units into subscripted parentheses, or as skeletal bond lines where vertices represent carbon atoms.
concepts.key_idea: In bond-line structures, line ends represent terminal methyl groups, vertices represent carbons with implied hydrogens, and heteroatoms are explicitly drawn.

concepts.title: Three-Dimensional Wedge-and-Dash Representation
concepts.definition: A 2D convention for illustrating 3D molecular stereochemistry where solid wedges signify bonds projecting toward the observer, dashed wedges indicate bonds pointing away, and normal lines denote bonds within the page plane.
concepts.key_idea: Solid wedges project forward out of the plane, dashed wedges point backward behind the plane, and plain lines lie within the plane.

solution_steps.action: locate bonds pointing away from the observer

concepts.title: Structural Classification of Organic Compounds
concepts.definition: Organic compounds are systematically categorized into open-chain aliphatic systems and closed-chain cyclic frameworks, with the latter further segregated into alicyclic and aromatic benzenoid, non-benzenoid, or heterocyclic types.
concepts.key_idea: Compounds are classified primarily by carbon skeleton connectivity into acyclic and cyclic structures, and secondarily by ring constitution into homocyclic and heterocyclic systems.

solution_steps.action: inspect ring atoms for elements other than carbon
solution_steps.explain: rings containing only carbon atoms are homocyclic; rings incorporating heteroatoms like N, O, or S are heterocyclic

solution_steps.action: assess aromatic character and benzenoid structure
solution_steps.explain: aromatic rings resembling benzene are benzenoid, while aromatic rings devoid of benzene units are non-benzenoid

concepts.title: Homologous Series and Molecular Mass Progression
concepts.definition: A homologous family comprises structurally similar organic compounds possessing the same characteristic functional group, in which any two adjacent members differ in constitution by one methylene unit.
concepts.key_idea: Consecutive homologues differ uniformly by a -CH2- unit, representing a fixed molecular mass discrepancy of 14 atomic mass units.

concepts.title: Hydrogen Content in Saturated Acyclic Alkanes
concepts.definition: Unbranched and branched open-chain alkanes are fully saturated hydrocarbons adhering to the stoichiometric relation where hydrogen atoms equal twice the carbon count plus two.
concepts.key_idea: Every acyclic saturated hydrocarbon contains 2n + 2 hydrogens for n carbon atoms.

solution_steps.action: verify the hydrogen count satisfies the general alkane formula

concepts.title: IUPAC Nomenclature of Branched Alkanes
concepts.definition: The systematic nomenclature of branched saturated hydrocarbons requires selecting the longest continuous carbon chain, numbering from the end providing lowest locants to substituents, and assembling substituent names alphabetically.
concepts.key_idea: The parent name comes from the longest continuous carbon sequence, numbered to assign lowest locant sets to branch points, alphabetizing substituent names irrespective of multiplying prefixes.

solution_steps.action: select the longest continuous carbon chain as the root alkane

solution_steps.action: number the root chain from the end closer to branch points
solution_steps.explain: apply the lowest locant rule at the first point of difference

solution_steps.action: assemble prefix names in alphabetical order with locants
solution_steps.explain: use hyphens between numerals and words, commas between numerals, and ignore prefixes like di or tri when alphabetizing

concepts.title: Principal Functional Group Priority in IUPAC Nomenclature
concepts.definition: In polyfunctional organic compounds, a seniority table determines the principal functional group providing the suffix ending, while all remaining lower-priority groups are cited as substituent prefixes.
concepts.key_idea: The highest priority functional group establishes the principal suffix, dictating lowest locant numbering of the parent carbon skeleton.
